entities.name: Albert-Léon-Marie Le Nordez
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Albert-Léon-Marie Le Nordez (1852–1905) was a French Catholic bishop whose episcopate of Dijon ended in one of the most sensational Church-state controversies in Third Republic France. Appointed Bishop of Dijon in 1899, he became embroiled in allegations that he had reported to the French government on clergy who had been sympathetic to Alfred Dreyfus, the Jewish army officer wrongly convicted of treason.

Le Nordez was accused of acting as a government informer against Catholic clergy who had defended Dreyfus, which placed him at the intersection of the Dreyfus Affair, anti-clerical republicanism, and internal Catholic politics. The accusations against him—whether fully proven or not—made him a figure of intense controversy within the French Church, accused of betrayal by clergy and conservative Catholics who saw the government as an enemy.

Pope Pius X, who had little patience for French Catholic accommodation with the Republic, eventually forced Le Nordez's resignation in 1905. The affair illustrated the extraordinary tensions within French Catholicism between those who sought some accommodation with the anticlerical republic ('ralliement') and those who saw any engagement with republican structures as betrayal. Le Nordez became, fairly or not, a symbol of the dangers of episcopal collaboration with an anticlerical state.
